notes: *What … is* goes to מִי as the verbless clause's predicate, on rule 20's מִי הָאִישׁ הַלָּזֶה → *What man is this* precedent; the further *he* is referential and answers to no morpheme, so it is `added`, with the competing reading treating *is he* as a single supplied frame named in the unit note.
הָיָה לְ is resultative: the copula belongs to the verb and the לְ is unrepresented (rule 21), while the second לְ takes its own *over*.
יֹשְׁבֵי is an anarthrous substantival participle taking the supplied *the* (rule 46), and כֹּל takes only *all*, no *of* being written between it and the following noun (rule 19).
